faqs.q: What is the current minimum wage in Australia per hour?
faqs.a: From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour for a full-time employee working 38 hours per week. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, making their minimum rate $33.05 per hour. These rates are set by the Fair Work Commission and apply to employees not covered by an award or agreement.

faqs.q: How much is the minimum wage per fortnight before tax?
faqs.a: For a full-time employee on the National Minimum Wage working 38 hours per week, the fortnightly pay before tax is $2,009.80 (that is $1,004.90 per week multiplied by 2). Casual employees on the minimum wage with the 25% loading earn $2,512.20 per fortnight before tax.

faqs.q: Does the minimum wage include superannuation?
faqs.a: No, superannuation is paid on top of the minimum wage. The employer must contribute an additional 12% of your ordinary earnings into your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a full-time minimum wage earner, that adds about $6,270.58 per year in super contributions.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the National Minimum Wage

If you are wondering **what is the current minimum wage in australia**, the answer depends on whether you are a full-time, part-time or casual employee. From 1 July 2026, the Fair Work Commission has set the National Minimum Wage at **$26.44 per hour** for a 38-hour week. This rate applies to employees who are not covered by an award or registered agreement.

For casual workers, the minimum wage includes a 25% casual loading, bringing the rate to **$33.05 per hour**. This loading compensates for entitlements that casuals do not receive, such as paid leave.

### How to Calculate Annual Pay from an Hourly Rate

The standard formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

When we assume a 38-hour week (the standard full-time week under the Fair Work Act), the calculation for the National Minimum Wage is:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = **$52,254.80 per year** before tax and super.

If you are a casual on the minimum wage, your annual gross pay would be:

$33.05 × 38 × 52 = **$65,318.80 per year** before tax and super.

Remember, this formula assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates or allowances. For a more personalised estimate, use [the timesheet](/) on our home page.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many Australians are paid fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by two. For a full-time minimum wage earner:

$1,004.90 per week × 2 = **$2,009.80 per fortnight** before tax.

For a casual minimum wage earner:

$1,256.10 per week × 2 = **$2,512.20 per fortnight** before tax.

Knowing your fortnightly figure helps with budgeting and comparing job offers.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor. However, many industries have **award rates** that are higher. Awards set minimum pay for specific jobs and can include penalty rates, shift allowances and overtime. Always check the relevant award for your occupation. Our [pay guides](/blog) can help you find the right award.

If you are covered by an award, your minimum hourly rate may be above $26.44. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides detailed information on award classifications.

### Casual Loading Explained

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. This is not extra pay for extra work; it compensates for not receiving paid sick leave, annual leave or public holiday pay. When using our calculator, do **not** type a rate that already includes casual loading. Instead, enter the base hourly rate and check the casual loading box to add 25% on top. For more details, see our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation (super) is an additional contribution your employer must make. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is **12% of your ordinary earnings**, paid on top of your gross pay. For a full-time minimum wage earner, that is an extra $6,270.58 per year (12% of $52,254.80), up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is paid into your super fund separately. Learn more on our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

### Tax on Minimum Wage Earnings

For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15c for each $1 over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30c for each $1 over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37c for each $1 over $135,000
- $190,001 and over: $51,367 plus 45c for each $1 over $190,000

Most taxpayers also pay a **Medicare levy of 2%** (with possible reductions for low incomes). For a full-time minimum wage earner on $52,254.80, the estimated tax (including Medicare) would be around $7,500–$8,000 per year, depending on your circumstances. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more accurate estimate.

### How Does the Minimum Wage Compare to Average Earnings?

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports that in May 2026, **full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings** were $2,083.70 per week. That is about $108,352 per year. The National Minimum Wage is significantly lower, reflecting its role as a safety net. The ABS also reports **all employees total earnings** (including part-time workers) at $1,579.20 per week. These are averages, not medians for any specific job. For job-specific pay data, see our [job pay](/topics/job-pay) page.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay shown here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Further Reading

For more detailed information, explore our [reference tables](/data) or read about [average pay](/topics/average-pay) across Australia. If you need to convert an annual salary to an hourly rate, visit our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page.
